summary: td is a task-management CLI and TUI designed primarily for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, etc.) operating in multi-session environments. It enforces session isolation for self-review prevention, provides structured handoffs between agent sessions, and surfaces a Linear-style kanban/swimlane TUI monitor. Secondary users are human developers managing AI agent workflows.

target_users.description: AI assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Qwen, OpenCode) running in terminal sessions that need structured task tracking, state handoff between context windows, and self-review prevention to maintain code quality.
key_needs: Structured state capture before context ends (handoff)
Optimized context output (td usage) for limited token budgets
Automatic session detection from environment variables
target_users.evidence: cmd/context.go (usage command generates optimized agent context), internal/session/session.go (auto-detects CLAUDE_CODE_SSE_PORT, CURSOR_SESSION_ID, CODEX_SESSION_ID, OPENCODE_SESSION_ID, QWEN_SESSION_ID), CLAUDE.md (mandatory td usage --new-session at conversation start)

target_users.description: Human developers who manage AI agent work, review agent-completed tasks, use the TUI monitor for visibility, and coordinate multi-agent workflows.
key_needs: Visual dashboard for tracking agent work (TUI monitor)
Board and swimlane views for project planning
Query language for filtering and searching issues
target_users.evidence: pkg/monitor/ (full TUI with mouse support, kanban, stats), cmd/review.go (approve/reject workflow), cmd/board.go (board management), cmd/query.go (TDQ query language)

target_users.description: A meta-agent (e.g., Oracle) that coordinates multiple sub-agents, assigns work, tracks progress, and manages epics across agents.
key_needs: Work session grouping for related issues
target_users.evidence: cmd/assign.go (agent assignment), cmd/activity.go (agent activity tracking), cmd/dependencies.go (critical-path command), cmd/epic.go and cmd/tree.go (hierarchy), cmd/ws.go (work sessions)

primary_jobs.title: Track work state across AI agent context windows
primary_jobs.description: When an AI agent's context window ends, it needs to capture what was done, what remains, key decisions, and uncertainties so the next session can resume without information loss.
primary_jobs.evidence: cmd/handoff.go (structured handoff with done/remaining/decisions/uncertain), cmd/context.go (usage generates optimized context block with handoff state), cmd/focus.go (check-handoff returns exit code 1 for agent hooks)

primary_jobs.title: Prevent self-review bypass in automated workflows
primary_jobs.description: Ensure that the AI session that implemented a change cannot also approve it. This enforces a minimum two-session review cycle to catch errors.
primary_jobs.evidence: cmd/review.go (WasSessionInvolved checks, creator/implementer session guards, --self-close-exception with security audit logging), internal/session/session.go (session scoped by branch + agent fingerprint)

primary_jobs.title: Manage issue lifecycle from creation to closure
primary_jobs.description: Full issue tracking with status transitions (open -> in_progress -> in_review -> closed, with blocked as a side state), type/priority/points categorization, labels, and sprint assignment.
primary_jobs.evidence: cmd/create.go, cmd/start.go, cmd/review.go, cmd/block.go, cmd/update.go, cmd/delete.go, internal/workflow/ (state machine with valid transition guards)

primary_jobs.title: Provide real-time visual dashboard for issue tracking
primary_jobs.description: A rich terminal UI (TUI) monitor with three panels (current work, task list, activity), modal issue details, board views (swimlanes, backlog, kanban), mouse support, and keyboard navigation.
primary_jobs.evidence: pkg/monitor/ (model.go, view.go, kanban.go, styles.go, types.go - full Bubble Tea TUI with 200+ Model fields)

primary_jobs.title: Organize and query issues with flexible filtering
primary_jobs.description: A custom query language (TDQ) supporting field comparisons, boolean operators, functions, cross-entity search, relative dates, and sorting. Plus full-text search and board-based views.
primary_jobs.evidence: cmd/query.go (full TDQ parser with 15+ fields, 8+ operators, 7+ functions), cmd/search.go (ranked full-text search), cmd/list.go (extensive filtering flags), cmd/board.go (query-based boards)

primary_jobs.title: Manage dependencies and identify critical path
primary_jobs.description: Track depends_on relationships between issues, visualize blocked trees, auto-unblock dependents on close, and compute critical path for optimal work ordering.
primary_jobs.evidence: cmd/dependencies.go (Kahn's algorithm weighted by block count for critical path, transitive dependency resolution)

primary_jobs.title: Coordinate multi-agent work on related issues
primary_jobs.description: Group related issues into work sessions, log progress across all tagged issues simultaneously, and generate per-issue handoffs at session end.
primary_jobs.evidence: cmd/ws.go (work session management with auto-start on tag, cascading handoffs, --review flag for bulk submission)

primary_jobs.title: Assign and track agent activity across issues
primary_jobs.description: Assign issues to named agents, track their activity (assigned, started, committed, pr_created, reviewed, completed, spawned_subagent, comment), and view agent activity logs.
primary_jobs.evidence: cmd/assign.go (assign/unassign), cmd/activity.go (view by issue or by agent), internal/models/models.go (AgentActivity struct with 8 activity types)

primary_jobs.title: Sync issue state across devices and agents
primary_jobs.description: Event-sourced synchronization with a remote server supporting push/pull, snapshot bootstrap for large projects, conflict detection, and auto-sync on mutations.
primary_jobs.evidence: cmd/sync.go (event-sourced sync with batching), cmd/autosync.go (debounced auto-sync on mutations and startup), cmd/sync_conflicts.go (conflict resolution), cmd/project.go (multi-user project management)

primary_jobs.title: Track progress with structured logging
primary_jobs.description: Record typed log entries (progress, blocker, decision, hypothesis, tried, result, orchestration) against issues for audit trail and context preservation.
primary_jobs.evidence: cmd/log.go (7 log types, flexible arg parsing, stdin support, auto-detects issue ID vs message)

primary_jobs.title: Manage epic hierarchies and parent-child relationships
primary_jobs.description: Create epics as container issues, add child tasks, visualize trees, and cascade status changes to descendants during review/handoff.
primary_jobs.evidence: cmd/epic.go, cmd/tree.go (tree visualization with depth control), cmd/review.go (cascade to descendants on review submission)

primary_jobs.title: Undo accidental changes
primary_jobs.description: Full undo system with action log snapshots that supports undoing create, delete, update, start, review, approve, reject, dependencies, file links, board positions, and handoffs.
primary_jobs.evidence: cmd/undo.go (action log with previous_data/new_data JSON snapshots, supports 20+ action types)

primary_jobs.title: Track files associated with issues
primary_jobs.description: Link files to issues with glob patterns, track SHA for change detection, and show file status (unchanged/modified/deleted/new) with untracked git changes.
primary_jobs.evidence: cmd/link.go (glob expansion, recursive directory linking, SHA-based change detection, git status integration)

primary_jobs.title: Import and export issue data
primary_jobs.description: Export full database to JSON or Markdown, import from JSON or Markdown with dry-run preview and force-overwrite support.
primary_jobs.evidence: cmd/system.go (export with format selection, import with JSON/Markdown parsing, dry-run, force overwrite)

user_flows.name: New AI Agent Session Startup
steps: 1. Agent starts new conversation
2. Runs `td usage --new-session` (mandatory per CLAUDE.md)
3. System auto-detects agent type from env vars (CLAUDE_CODE_SSE_PORT, etc.)
4. New session created (or rotated if stale)
5. Optimized context block returned with: focused issue, handoff state, reviewable issues, ready work, instructions
6. Agent reads context and resumes work or picks next task

user_flows.name: Implement and Submit Work
steps: 1. `td next` or `td critical-path` to identify work
2. `td start <id>` captures git state and moves to in_progress
3. `td log 'progress message'` during work
4. `td log --decision 'chose X because Y'` for key decisions
5. `td link <id> src/changed/*.go` to track modified files
6. `td handoff <id> --done '...' --remaining '...'` before context ends
7. `td review <id>` to submit for review

user_flows.name: Review and Approve Work
steps: 1. Different session runs `td reviewable` to see available reviews
2. `td show <id>` to examine issue details, logs, handoff, diff stats
3. `td approve <id>` if acceptable (self-review prevention enforced)
4. OR `td reject <id> --reason '...'` to return for rework
5. On approve: issue closed, dependents auto-unblocked

user_flows.name: Multi-Issue Work Session
steps: 1. `td ws start 'Auth implementation'` creates work session
2. `td ws tag <id1> <id2>` associates and auto-starts issues
3. `td ws log 'shared progress'` logs to all tagged issues
4. `td ws handoff --review` generates per-issue handoffs and submits all
5. `td ws end` closes the work session

user_flows.name: Board Management and Visualization
steps: 1. `td board create 'Sprint' --query 'priority <= P1'` creates query-based board
2. TUI monitor opens board in swimlanes, backlog, or kanban view
3. Navigate with keyboard (h/l for columns, j/k for cards in kanban)
4. Press 'v' to cycle view modes (swimlanes -> backlog -> kanban)
5. Enter opens issue modal with full details
6. `td board move <board> <id> <position>` for manual ordering

user_flows.name: Dependency Analysis and Unblocking
steps: 1. `td dep add <issue> <depends-on>` to declare dependency
2. `td critical-path` shows optimal unblocking sequence
3. Work on highest-impact issue first
4. On close/approve, dependents auto-unblock
5. `td blocked-by <id>` shows full transitive blocked tree

user_flows.name: Project Sync Setup
steps: 1. `td feature set sync_cli true` enables sync feature
2. `td auth login` authenticates with device code flow
3. `td project create <name>` or `td project join <id>` to connect
4. `td sync push` / `td sync pull` for manual sync
5. Auto-sync runs on mutations and at monitor startup if configured
6. `td doctor` diagnoses sync issues

competitive_advantage.description: Unlike general-purpose issue trackers, td is designed from the ground up for AI coding agents. Session auto-detection, handoff protocols, context optimization (td usage), and check-handoff hooks are unique to AI agent workflows.
competitive_advantage.evidence: internal/session/session.go (5 agent types detected), cmd/context.go (optimized context generation)

competitive_advantage.description: Enforces that the session implementing a change cannot approve it, preventing rubber-stamp reviews in automated workflows. This is a critical safety feature for AI-generated code.
First-class handoff primitives (done/remaining/decisions/uncertain) that bridge context windows. No other task tracker has this built-in.
A purpose-built query language with cross-entity search, relative dates, session references, and functions. More powerful than Linear/Jira JQL for the CLI context.
A full-featured terminal UI with kanban boards, mouse support, stacked modals, drag-to-resize panels, and Linear-matching color scheme. Runs in any terminal without a browser.
Monitor can be embedded in external applications (sidecar) with custom renderers, themes, and connection pooling. No other CLI task tracker offers this.
Full sync infrastructure with conflict detection, snapshot bootstrap, and auto-sync. Designed for multi-agent collaboration across devices.
Automatically identifies the AI agent type from environment variables (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Qwen, OpenCode) without any user configuration.

missing_jobs.title: No time tracking or estimation vs actual comparison
missing_jobs.description: Issues have story points but no time estimates or actual time tracking. Cannot compare estimated effort vs actual for velocity calculations.

missing_jobs.title: No notification or webhook system
missing_jobs.description: No mechanism to notify agents or humans when issues are assigned, reviewed, blocked, or updated. Agents must poll (td usage) to discover changes.
missing_jobs.who_wants_it: Orchestrator agents needing real-time event awareness

missing_jobs.title: No issue templates or recurring tasks
missing_jobs.description: No way to create issue templates for common patterns (bug report template, feature template) or define recurring tasks that auto-create on schedule.

missing_jobs.title: No git branch/PR linkage beyond snapshot
missing_jobs.description: Git snapshots capture state at start/handoff but there is no explicit PR tracking or branch-to-issue mapping beyond the created_branch field. Agent activity has pr_created type but no automated detection.

missing_jobs.title: No multi-project support in single database
missing_jobs.description: Each project directory has its own .todos/issues.db. There is a project_tag field but no cross-project views or unified dashboard.

missing_jobs.title: No configurable workflow state machine
missing_jobs.description: The state machine (open -> in_progress -> in_review -> closed) is hardcoded. Custom statuses or transition rules are not supported.
missing_jobs.who_wants_it: Teams with custom workflows (e.g., QA stage, staging, deployment)

missing_jobs.title: No rich attachment support
missing_jobs.description: File links track paths and SHAs but there is no support for screenshots, images, or binary attachments on issues.
missing_jobs.who_wants_it: Bug reporters needing to attach screenshots

missing_jobs.title: Limited Linear integration
missing_jobs.description: Issues have linear_id and linear_identifier fields, suggesting planned Linear sync, but no bidirectional sync commands exist in the CLI. The sync system is generic event-sourced, not Linear-specific.
missing_jobs.who_wants_it: Teams using Linear as their primary tracker who want td as an agent-side companion

half_implemented_features.description: Issue model has LinearID and LinearIdentifier fields. Activity log shows identifiers in display. But no commands exist to sync with Linear API. The sync system is for td-to-td sync, not Linear sync.
half_implemented_features.evidence: internal/models/models.go (LinearID, LinearIdentifier fields), cmd/activity.go (linearInfo display), no linear sync commands in cmd/

half_implemented_features.description: TDQ has stale(N) function for finding issues not updated in N days. However, there is no automated stale notification or dashboard widget highlighting stale issues.
half_implemented_features.evidence: cmd/query.go (stale function documented in TDQ help)

half_implemented_features.description: Issues have a sprint field that can be set via update, but there are no sprint management commands (create sprint, close sprint, sprint burndown, sprint planning).
SendTaskToWorktreeMsg is defined in TUI types for embedding contexts to intercept, suggesting planned worktree-per-issue workflows. But no command-level worktree management exists.
LogTypeOrchestration exists as a log type but there is no special handling, display, or queries specific to orchestration logs.
